Text 1

The longest bull run in a century of art-market history ended on a dramatic note with a sale of 56 works by Damien Hirst, Beautiful Inside My Head Forever, at Sotheby's in London on September 15th 2008.
sentences.translation: 2008年9月15日，达米恩·赫斯特的56件作品以“美丽永驻我心”为名在伦敦苏富比拍卖，艺术市场百年来持续时间最长的牛市以戏剧性的方式落幕。

sentences.english: All but two pieces sold, fetching more than £70m, a record for a sale by a single artist.
sentences.translation: 除两件外，作品全部售出，成交额超过七千万英镑，创下单一艺术家拍卖纪录。

sentences.english: It was a last victory.
sentences.translation: 这是最后一次胜利。

sentences.english: As the auctioneer called out bids, in New York one of the oldest banks on Wall Street, Lehman Brothers, filed for bankruptcy.
sentences.translation: 就在拍卖师喊价时，纽约华尔街历史最悠久的银行之一雷曼兄弟申请了破产。

sentences.english: The world art market had already been losing momentum for a while after rising bewilderingly since 2003.
sentences.translation: 全球艺术市场自2003年以来经历了令人眼花缭乱的上涨后，增长势头其实已经减弱了一段时间。

sentences.english: At its peak in 2007 it was worth some $65 billion, reckons Clare McAndrew, founder of Arts Economics, a research firm - double the figure five years earlier.
sentences.translation: 研究机构Arts Economics创始人克莱尔·麦克安德鲁估计，市场在2007年达到顶峰，规模约为650亿美元，是五年前的两倍。

sentences.english: Since then it may have come down to $50 billion.
sentences.translation: 此后，市场规模可能已经降至500亿美元。

sentences.english: But the market generates interest far beyond its size because it brings together great wealth, enormous egos, greed, passion and controversy m a way matched by few other industries.
In the weeks and months that followed Mr. Hirst's sale, spending of any sort became deeply unfashionable.
sentences.translation: 赫斯特的拍卖结束后的数周乃至数月里，各类消费都变得十分不合时宜。

sentences.english: In the art world that meant collectors stayed away from galleries and salerooms.
sentences.translation: 在艺术界，这意味着收藏家不再光顾画廊和拍卖场。

sentences.english: Sales of contemporary art fell by two-thirds, and in the most overheated sector, they were down by nearly 90% in the year to November 2008.
sentences.translation: 当代艺术品销售额下降了三分之二；在市场最过热的领域，截至2008年11月的一年里，降幅接近90%。

sentences.english: Within weeks the world's two biggest auction houses, Sotheby's and Christie's, had to pay out nearly $200m in guarantees to clients who had placed works for sale with them.
sentences.translation: 短短数周内，全球最大的两家拍卖行苏富比和佳士得，不得不向委托其出售作品的客户支付近两亿美元的担保款。

sentences.english: The current downturn in the art market is the worst since the Japanese stopped buying Impressionists at the end of 1989.
sentences.translation: 目前艺术市场的衰退，是自日本买家于1989年底停止购买印象派作品以来最严重的一次。

sentences.english: This time experts reckon that prices are about 40% down on their peak on average, though some have been far more fluctuant.
sentences.translation: 专家估计，这次价格比峰值平均下跌约40%，不过部分作品的价格波动要大得多。

sentences.english: But Edward Dolman, Christie's chief executive, says: "I'm pretty confident we're at the bottom."
sentences.translation: 但佳士得首席执行官爱德华·多尔曼说：“我相当确信，我们已经处于谷底了。”

sentences.english: What makes this slump different from the last, he says, is that there are still buyers in the market.
sentences.translation: 他说，这次衰退与上一次不同之处在于，市场上仍然有买家。

sentences.english: Almost everyone who was interviewed for this special report said that the biggest problem at the moment is not a lack of demand but a lack of good work to sell.
sentences.translation: 几乎所有接受本篇专题报道采访的人都表示，目前最大的问题并非缺乏需求，而是缺少可供出售的好作品。

sentences.english: The three Ds - death, debt and divorce - still deliver works of art to the market.
sentences.translation: 死亡、债务和离婚这三个以D开头的因素，仍会促使艺术品流入市场。

sentences.english: But anyone who does not have to sell is keeping away, waiting for confidence to return.
sentences.translation: 但没有迫切出售需求的人都在观望，等待市场信心恢复。

Text2 I was addressing a small gathering in a suburban Virginia living room - a women's group that had invited men to join them.
Throughout the evening, one man had been particularly talkative, frequently offering ideas and anecdotes, while his wife sat silently beside him on the couch.
sentences.translation: 整个晚上，一名男子格外健谈，不断发表意见、讲述趣事，而他的妻子默默地坐在他旁边的沙发上。

sentences.english: Toward the end of the evening, I commented that women frequently complain that their husbands don't talk to them.
sentences.translation: 聚会快结束时，我谈到女性常常抱怨丈夫不和她们说话。

sentences.english: This man quickly nodded in agreement.
sentences.translation: 这名男子立刻点头表示赞同。

sentences.english: He gestured toward his wife and said, "She's the talker in our family."
sentences.translation: 他指向妻子说：“在我们家，她才是爱说话的人。”

sentences.english: The room burst into laughter; the man looked puzzled and hurt.
sentences.translation: 屋里的人突然大笑起来；那名男子显得困惑又委屈。

sentences.english: "It's true," he explained.
sentences.translation: “这是真的，”他解释道。

sentences.english: "When I come home from work I have nothing to say.
sentences.translation: “我下班回到家就没什么话可说了。

sentences.english: If she didn't keep the conversation going, we'd spend the whole evening in silence."
sentences.translation: 要不是她一直找话说，我们整个晚上都会一言不发。”

sentences.english: This episode crystallizes the irony that although American men tend to talk more than women in public situations, they often talk less at home.
sentences.translation: 这个片段鲜明地呈现出一种反差：美国男性在公共场合往往比女性话多，在家里却常常话少。

sentences.english: And this pattern is wreaking havoc with marriage.
sentences.translation: 而这种模式正对婚姻造成严重损害。

sentences.english: The pattern was observed by political scientist Andrew Hacker in the late 1970s.
sentences.translation: 政治学家安德鲁·哈克在20世纪70年代末就注意到了这种模式。

sentences.english: Sociologist Catherine Kohler Riessman reports in her new book Divorce Talk that most of the women she interviewed - but only a few of the men - gave lack of communication as the reason for their divorces.
sentences.translation: 社会学家凯瑟琳·科勒·里斯曼在新书《离婚谈》中指出，受访女性大多把缺乏沟通作为离婚原因，而男性中只有少数这样说。

sentences.english: Given the current divorce rate of nearly 50 percent, that amounts to millions of cases in the United States every year a virtual epidemic of failed conversation.
sentences.translation: 考虑到目前接近50%的离婚率，这在美国每年就涉及数百万个案例，几乎成了一场沟通失败的流行病。

sentences.english: In my own research, complaints from women about their husbands most often focused not on tangible inequities such as having given up the chance for a career to accompany a husband to his, or doing far more than their share of daily life-support work like cleaning, cooking and social arrangements.
sentences.translation: 在我自己的研究中，女性对丈夫的抱怨大多不集中于具体的不平等，比如放弃自己的事业陪伴丈夫发展，或在打扫、做饭、安排社交等日常事务中承担远超应有份额的劳动。

sentences.english: Instead, they focused on communication: "He doesn't listen to me."
"He doesn't talk to me."
I found, as Hacker observed years before, that most wives want their husbands to be, first and foremost, conversational partners, but few husbands share this expectation of their wives.
sentences.translation: 正如哈克多年前观察到的，我发现多数妻子首先希望丈夫是能与自己交谈的伙伴，但很少有丈夫对妻子抱有同样的期待。

sentences.english: In short, the image that best represents the current crisis is the stereotypical cartoon scene of a man sitting at the breakfast table with a newspaper held up in front of his face, while a woman glares at the back of it, wanting to talk.
sentences.translation: 简而言之，最能表现当前危机的，是这样一幅典型漫画：男人坐在早餐桌前，举着报纸遮住脸；女人怒视着报纸的背面，想要说话。

[A] Talking to them.
[B] Trusting them. [C] Supporting their careers.
[D] Sharing housework.

Text3 Over the past decade, many compames had perfected the art of creating automatic behaviors - habits - among consumers.
These habits have helped companies earn billions of dollars when customers eat snacks or wipe counters almost without thinking, often in response to a carefully designed set of daily cues.
sentences.translation: 消费者吃零食、擦台面时几乎不假思索，常常是在回应一套精心设计的日常提示；这些习惯帮助企业赚取了数十亿美元。

sentences.english: "There are fundamental public health problems, like dirty hands instead of a soap habit, that remain killers only because we can't figure out how to change people's habits," said Dr. Curtis, the director of the Hygiene Center at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine.
sentences.translation: 伦敦卫生与热带医学院卫生中心主任柯蒂斯博士说，一些基本公共卫生问题，例如不用肥皂洗手、让手保持脏污，仍在致人死亡，原因就在于人们还没找到改变行为习惯的方法。

sentences.english: "We wanted to learn from private industry how to create new behaviors that happen automatically."
sentences.translation: 她说，我们希望向私营企业学习，了解如何让人们自然而然地形成新的行为。

sentences.english: The companies that Dr. Curtis turned to - Procter & Gamble, Colgate- Palmolive and Unilever - had invested hundreds of millions of dollars finding the subtle cues in consumers' lives that corporations could use to introduce new routines.
sentences.translation: 柯蒂斯博士求助的宝洁、高露洁棕榄和联合利华，已经投入数亿美元，寻找消费者生活中那些企业可以利用来引入新习惯的细微提示。

sentences.english: If you look hard enough, you'll find that many of the products we use every day - chewing gums, skin moisturizers, disinfecting wipes, air fresheners, water purifiers, health snacks, teeth whiteners, fabric softeners, vitamins - are results of manufactured habits.
sentences.translation: 仔细观察就会发现，许多日用品——口香糖、润肤品、消毒湿巾、空气清新剂、净水器、健康零食、牙齿美白剂、衣物柔顺剂和维生素——都是人为塑造习惯的结果。

sentences.english: A century ago, few people regularly brushed their teeth multiple times a day.
sentences.translation: 一个世纪前，很少有人习惯每天刷牙多次。

sentences.english: Today, because of shrewd advertising and public health campaigns, many Americans habitually give their pearly whites a cavity-preventing scrub twice a day, often with Colgate, Crest or one of the other brands.
sentences.translation: 如今，由于精明的广告和公共卫生宣传，许多美国人习惯每天两次清洁洁白的牙齿以防蛀牙，常常使用高露洁、佳洁士或其他品牌。

sentences.english: A few decades ago, many people didn't drink water outside of a meal.
sentences.translation: 几十年前，许多人不在用餐时间以外喝水。

sentences.english: Then beverage companies started bottling the production of far-off springs, and now office workers unthinkingly sip bottled water all day long.
sentences.translation: 后来，饮料公司开始把远方的泉水装瓶销售，如今办公室职员会整天不假思索地喝瓶装水。

sentences.english: Chewing gum, once bought primarily by adolescent boys, is now featured in commercials as a breath freshener and teeth cleanser for use after a meal.
sentences.translation: 口香糖过去主要由青春期男孩购买，如今广告将它宣传成饭后清新口气、清洁牙齿的用品。

sentences.english: Skin moisturizers are advertised as part of morning beauty rituals, slipped in between hair brushing and putting on makeup.
sentences.translation: 润肤品被宣传为早晨美容程序的一部分，安排在梳头与化妆之间使用。

sentences.english: "Our products succeed when they become part of daily or weekly patterns," said Carol Berning, a consumer psychologist who recently retired from Procter & Gamble, the company that sold $76 billion of Tide, Crest and other products last year.
sentences.translation: 刚从宝洁退休的消费心理学家卡萝尔·伯宁说，当产品成为人们每日或每周生活模式的一部分时，它们就成功了；宝洁去年销售了760亿美元的汰渍、佳洁士等产品。

sentences.english: "Creating positive habits is a huge part of improving our consumers' lives, and it's essential to making new products commercially viable."
sentences.translation: 她说，培养积极习惯是改善消费者生活的重要部分，也是让新产品在商业上可行的关键。

sentences.english: Through experiments and observation, social scientists like Dr. Berning have learned that there is power in tying certain behaviors to habitual cues through ruthless advertising.
sentences.translation: 通过实验和观察，伯宁等社会科学家认识到，利用强势广告将某些行为与习惯性提示关联起来，会产生强大作用。

sentences.english: As this new science of habit has emerged, controversies have erupted when the tactics have been used to sell questionable beauty creams or unhealthy foods.
sentences.translation: 随着这门关于习惯的新科学兴起，当这些手法被用于推销效果存疑的美容霜或不健康的食品时，争议也随之爆发。

[A] should be further cultivated [B] should be changed gradually [C] are deeply rooted in history [D] are basically private concerns

[C] Colgate. [D] Unilever.

[A] indifferent [B] negative [C] positive [D] biased - 8 -

Text4 Many Americans regard the jury system as a concrete express10n of crucial democratic values, including the principles that all citizens who meet minimal qualifications of age and literacy are equally competent to serve on juries; that jurors should be selected randomly from a representative cross section of the community; that no citizen should be denied the right to serve on a jury on account of race, religion, sex, or national origin; that defendants are entitled to trial by their peers; and that verdicts should represent
the conscience of the community and not just the letter of the law.
The jury is also said to be the best surviving example of direct rather than representative democracy.
sentences.translation: 陪审团还被认为是现存直接民主，而非代议民主，最好的范例。

sentences.english: In a direct democracy, citizens take turns governing themselves, rather than electing representatives to govern for them.
sentences.translation: 在直接民主中，公民轮流管理自身事务，而不是选出代表代为治理。

sentences.english: But as recently as in 1968, jury selection procedures conflicted with these democratic ideals.
sentences.translation: 然而，直到1968年，陪审员的选拔程序仍与这些民主理想相冲突。

sentences.english: In some states, for example, jury duty was limited to persons of supposedly superior intelligence, education, and moral character.
sentences.translation: 例如，有些州把陪审职责限定给那些被认为在智力、教育和道德品质方面更优秀的人。

sentences.english: Although the Supreme Court of the United States had prohibited intentional racial discrimination in jury selection as early as the 1880 case of Strauder v.
West Virginia, the practice of selecting so-called elite or blue-ribbon juries provided a convenient way around this and other antidiscrimination laws.
The system also failed to regularly include women on juries until the mid-20th century.
sentences.translation: 直到20世纪中叶，这一制度仍未能让女性常规性地参与陪审团。

sentences.english: Although women first served on state juries in Utah in 1898, it was not until the 1940s that a majority of states made women eligible for jury duty.
sentences.translation: 虽然犹他州早在1898年就有女性担任州法院陪审员，但直到20世纪40年代，大多数州才允许女性承担陪审职责。

sentences.english: Even then several states automatically exempted women from jury duty unless they personally asked to have their names included on the jury list.
sentences.translation: 即便如此，仍有几个州自动免除女性的陪审义务，除非女性本人要求把自己的名字列入陪审员名单。

sentences.english: This practice was justified by the claim that women were needed at home, and it kept juries unrepresentative of women through the 1960s.
sentences.translation: 这种做法以家庭需要女性为理由，导致直到20世纪60年代，陪审团仍缺乏女性代表。

sentences.english: In 1968, the Congress of the United States passed the Jury Selection and Service Act, ushering in a new era of democratic reforms for the jury.
sentences.translation: 1968年，美国国会通过《陪审员选拔与服务法》，开启了陪审团民主改革的新时期。

sentences.english: This law abolished special educational requirements for federal jurors and required them to be selected at random from a cross section of the entire community.
sentences.translation: 该法取消了对联邦陪审员的特殊教育要求，并规定须从整个社区的各类人群中随机选取。

sentences.english: In the landmark 1975 decision Taylor v.
Louisiana, the Supreme Court extended the requirement that juries be representative of all parts of the community to the state level.
The Taylor decision also declared sex discrimination in jury selection to be unconstitutional and ordered states to use the same procedures for selecting male and female jurors.
sentences.translation: 泰勒案的裁决还宣布，陪审员选拔中的性别歧视违反宪法，并命令各州采用相同程序选拔男性与女性陪审员。

PartB Directions: Read the following text and decide whether each of the statements is true or false.
Choose T if the statement is true or F if the statement is not true.
Mark your answers on ANSWER SHEET 1.
(10 points) Copying Birds May Save Aircraft Fuel Both Boeing and Airbus have trumpeted the efficiency of their newest aircraft, the 787 and A350 respectively.
Their clever designs and lightweight composites certainly make a difference.

But a group of researchers at Stanford University, led by Ilan Kroo, has suggested that airlines could take a more naturalistic approach to cutting jet-fuel use and it would not require them to buy new aircraft.
The answer, says Dr. Kroo, lies with birds.
Since 1914, scientists have known that birds flying in formation - a V-shape - expend less energy.
The air flowing over a bird's wings curls upwards behind the wingtips, a phenomenon known as upwash.
Other birds flying in the upwash experience reduced drag, and spend less energy propelling themselves.
Peter Lissaman, an aeronautics expert who was formerly at Caltech and the University of Southern California, has suggested that a formation of 25 birds might enjoy a range increase of71 %.
When applied to aircraft, the principles are not substantially different.

Dr. Kroo and his team modeled what would happen if three passenger jets departing from Los Angeles, San Francisco and Las Vegas were to assemble over Utah, assume an inverted V-formation, occasionally change places so all could have a tum in the most favourable positions, and proceed to London.
They found that the aircraft consumed as much as 15% less fuel (coupled with a reduction in carbon-dioxide output).
Nitrogen-oxide emissions during the cruising portions of the flight fell by around a quarter.
There are, of course, knots to be worked out.
One consideration is safety, or at least the perception of it.
Would passengers feel comfortable travelling in companion?
Dr. Kroo points out that the aircraft could be separated by several nautical miles, and would not be in the intimate groupings favoured by display teams like the Red Arrows.
A passenger peering out of the window might not even see the other planes.

Whether the separation distances involved would satisfy air-traffic-control regulations is another matter, although a working group at the International Civil Aviation Organisation has included the possibility of formation flying in a blueprint for new operational guidelines.
It remains to be seen how weather conditions affect the air flows that make formation flight more efficient.
In zones of increased turbulence, the planes' wakes will decay more quickly and the effect will diminish.
Dr. Kroo says this is one of the areas his team will investigate further.
It might also be hard for airlines to co-ordinate the departure times and destinations of passenger aircraft in a way that would allow them to gain from formation flight.
Cargo aircraft, in contrast, might be easier to reschedule, as might routine military flights.
As it happens, America's armed forces are on the case already.
Earlier this year the country's Defence Advanced Research Projects Agency announced plans to pay Boeing to investigate formation flight, though the programme has yet to begin.
There are reports that some military aircraft flew in formation when they were low on fuel during the Second World War, but Dr. Lissaman says they are unsubstantiated.
"My father was an RAF pilot and my cousin the skipper of a Lancaster lost over Berlin," he adds.
So he should know.
41. Findings of the Stanford University researchers will promote the sales of new Boeing and Airbus aircraft.
42. The upwash experience may save propelling energy as wellas reducing resistance.
43. Formation flight is more comfortable because passengers can not see the other planes.
44. The role that weather plays in formation flight has not yet been clearly defined.
45. It has been documented that during World War II, America's armed forces once tried formation flight to save fuel.

(15 points) "Sustainability" has become a popular word these days, but to Ted Ning, the concept will always have personal meaning.
Having endured a painful period of unsustainability in his own life made it clear to him that sustainability-oriented values must be expressed through everyday action and choice.
Ning recalls spending a confusing year in the late 1990s selling insurance.
He'd been through the dot-corn boom and burst and, desperate for a job, signed on with a Boulder agency.
It didn't go well.
"It was a really bad move because that's not my passion," says Ning, whose dilemma about the job translated, predictably, into a lack of sales.
"I was miserable. I had so much anxiety that I would wake up in the middle of the night and stare at the ceiling.
I had no money and needed the job.
Everyone said, 'Just wait, you'll turn the comer, give it some time."'
